plans.buy_case: DECK is flashing a textbook mean-reversion setup: RSI at exactly 30 with a bullish divergence (higher RSI low against a lower price low), price compressing near the lower Bollinger Band during a squeeze, and MACD histogram turning up from a valley. The golden cross remains intact and HOKA's brand momentum gives fundamental backing to what the technicals are already screaming — this is a quality company on sale, not a falling knife.
plans.entry_condition: Enter at market open or on any intraday dip toward $98–100. If RSI ticks below 28 intraday, that's an even better fill — add aggressively. Do not chase above $103 without a confirmed close above 50MA.
plans.exit_condition: Exit when RSI reaches 60–65, price tags the upper Bollinger Band, or a clean close above $118. Cut the trade if price closes below $93.50 (prior price low) — that invalidates the divergence thesis entirely.
plans.risk: Consumer cyclical sentiment can deteriorate fast if macro data weakens (e.g. soft retail sales print or rising unemployment). Price is also still technically below the 200MA ($103.51) and 50MA ($104.31), meaning those levels become resistance before becoming support — a failed breakout through $104 would be a warning sign.

plans.buy_case: GRMN is flashing a textbook mean-reversion setup: RSI at 25.7 with bullish divergence (price made a lower low but RSI made a higher low), price hugging the lower Bollinger Band during a squeeze, and MACD histogram turning up from a valley. The stock remains above its 200MA and holds a golden cross structure, meaning you're buying a short-term oversold dip within a healthy longer-term uptrend — exactly the risk/reward profile your strategy is built for.
plans.entry_condition: Enter at market open or on any intraday dip toward $236–$240. Do not chase if price gaps above $245 before entry — wait for a pullback. Confirm MACD histogram is still curling upward on the day of entry.
plans.exit_condition: Exit when RSI reaches 60–65 (mean-reversion complete), price touches the upper Bollinger Band, or MACD histogram rolls back over to the downside after a sustained rally. Hard stop-loss at $224 (just below the 200MA — if it loses this level, the thesis is broken).
plans.risk: A broader market selloff (VIX spike) could drag GRMN lower even if the company-specific setup is sound. The BB squeeze can resolve to the downside, and with only 4 shares your stop at $224 represents roughly a $64 loss (~1.8% of portfolio) — manageable but verify current earnings calendar to avoid holding through an unplanned catalyst.

plans.buy_case: TPL is flashing a textbook mean-reversion setup: RSI at 23.1 is deep in oversold territory, price is hugging the lower Bollinger Band with an active squeeze, and the stock remains above its 200MA — confirming the long-term uptrend is intact. The golden cross (50MA at 471.60 > 200MA at 359.65) adds structural bullish confirmation, meaning this dip is likely a shakeout within a healthy trend rather than a breakdown. TPL's asset-light Permian royalty model is fundamentally durable, giving this trade both technical and fundamental backing.
plans.entry_condition: Enter at market open or on a limit order near current price (~$394). Ideally, wait for a 1-2 day stabilization candle (small-bodied or bullish reversal candle on the daily chart) confirming sellers are exhausted before pulling the trigger. Do not chase if price surges more than 3% before you enter.
plans.exit_condition: Exit when RSI reclaims the 55-65 zone OR price approaches the 50MA (~$471), whichever comes first. Also exit if price closes more than 2 consecutive days below the 200MA (359.65), which would invalidate the setup. Tighten stop mentally to a daily close below $370 (~6% drawdown) to protect capital.
plans.risk: TPL carries meaningful commodity-price sensitivity — a sharp drop in oil/gas prices or broader energy sector selloff could push the stock lower despite the oversold signal. The stretched valuation (premium multiples) also means limited margin of safety if fundamentals disappoint, and with only 2 shares, a prolonged drawdown ties up capital with limited flexibility to average down.

plans.buy_case: PCG is flashing a textbook mean-reversion setup with RSI at 21.4 (deeply oversold), price hugging the lower Bollinger Band, and MACD histogram turning up from a valley — all classic signs of exhausted selling pressure. The Bollinger squeeze adds fuel: when the band expands, the move tends to be sharp and fast. With a golden cross intact (50MA above 200MA) and price essentially sitting on the 200MA as support, the technical risk/reward strongly favors a bounce toward the mid-band.
plans.entry_condition: Enter at market open or on any intraday dip toward $15.80–$16.10. Do NOT chase if price gaps up more than 2% before you can execute. Confirm MACD histogram is still turning positive before pulling the trigger.
plans.exit_condition: Exit when RSI climbs back above 55, price touches the upper Bollinger Band, or when price reaches the 50MA (~$17.51). Also exit immediately if price closes below $15.30 (stop-loss — that's your hard floor, no exceptions).
plans.risk: PCG carries real structural risk: leveraged balance sheet, wildfire liability overhang, and heavy California regulatory dependence. Any negative headline — a new wildfire, adverse CPUC ruling, or credit downgrade — can gap this stock down hard and fast, blowing through technical support. This is NOT a clean utility; it's a quasi-distressed turnaround story dressed in utility clothes. The stop at $15.30 is non-negotiable.

plans.buy_case: EXPE is flashing a textbook mean-reversion setup: RSI at 25.1 is deeply oversold, price is hugging the lower Bollinger Band with a squeeze active, and volume is running at 2.47x average — signaling capitulation selling rather than distribution. plans.exit_condition: Take profit when RSI crosses above 60, price tags the 50MA (~$239) or upper Bollinger Band (~$247), whichever comes first. Cut losses with a hard stop at $218 (approximately 4.5% downside) — no exceptions.
